goal: What are the main differences between SQLite and PostgreSQL for a small web app? Give sources.

solo.title: Single agent does everything

findings.title: Architecture: embedded vs client-server
findings.detail: SQLite is an embedded, serverless single-file library; PostgreSQL is a client-server RDBMS needing install and administration.

evidence.quote:
Type
Embedded, serverless (single file)
Client-server RDBMS

findings.title: Concurrency model
findings.detail: SQLite allows a single writer with file-level locking; PostgreSQL uses MVCC supporting many concurrent readers and writers.

evidence.quote:
Concurrency
Single writer, file-level locking
High (MVCC, many concurrent writers)

findings.title: Setup and operational overhead
findings.detail: SQLite is zero-config with no server process; PostgreSQL must be installed, configured, and administered.

evidence.quote:
Setup
Zero-config, no server
Install, configure, and administer

findings.title: Best-fit use cases
findings.detail: SQLite suits embedded apps, mobile, prototyping, and edge; PostgreSQL suits multi-user, enterprise, and complex-query workloads.

evidence.quote:
Best for
Embedded apps, mobile, prototyping, edge
Multi-user, enterprise, complex queries

findings.title: Scalability
findings.detail: SQLite targets small-to-medium local data; PostgreSQL scales to large datasets and high load.

evidence.quote:
Scale
Small to medium, local
Large datasets, high load

findings.title: SQL feature support
findings.detail: SQLite supports advanced SQL (partial indexes, JSON, window functions, recursive queries) but PostgreSQL has broader extensibility and richer features.

evidence.quote:
Full-Featured SQL Implementation:
Despite its lightweight design, SQLite supports
advanced SQL features
including partial indexes, comprehensive JSON handling, window functions, and recursive queries

findings.title: ACID compliance
findings.detail: Both provide ACID transactions; SQLite implements complete serializable ACID transactions.

evidence.quote:
ACID Transactions:
SQLite implements complete serializable
ACID transactions

findings.title: Licensing
findings.detail: SQLite is public domain; PostgreSQL uses a permissive open-source license.

evidence.quote:
License
Public domain
Permissive open-source (PostgreSQL License)

solo.summary: For a small web app, the main differences are architecture, concurrency, and operational overhead. SQLite is an embedded, serverless, single-file database library with zero configuration, ideal for lightweight/prototyping apps, but it uses file-level locking with a single writer at a time. PostgreSQL is a client-server RDBMS that requires installation and administration, but offers high concurrency via MVCC (many concurrent readers/writers), richer SQL features, and scales to large datasets and high load. For a small app with modest traffic, SQLite is simpler and faster to deploy; if you expect concurrent writes, complex queries, or growth, PostgreSQL is the safer choice.
